Cc: Elmbridge Ops <ops@elmbridge.ai>

Subject: Production: private cluster p95 spike + 500s on /generate — urgent

Hi Michael,

We're seeing a sustained p95 latency jump from ~420ms to ~2.4s across our VPC deployment starting ~08:30 PDT, and intermittently a spike of 500s on the /generate endpoint. Error rate (5xx) has moved from 0.2% to ~3.1% in the last 40 minutes.

We've attached a tar of recent logs (elmbridge_error_logs_0518.zip) and a short stacktrace bundle. Key points from our side:
- No infra changes on our end in the last 48h; autoscaler reports nodes healthy.
- Memory and GPU metrics look normal; CPU on the CPU-side translator is elevated.
- Replays of the failing request IDs show long decode stalls (~1.8s) before kernel execution.

CFO wants to understand expected customer impact; ops is asking for an immediate mitigation plan and an executive sync if this will take more than 2 hours to resolve. Can Redwood confirm whether this is a known regression (recent quantization / kernel change), and what quick roll-back or canary we can run?

Dana
Elmbridge AI — Sr. VP, Infrastructure

Attachments: elmbridge_error_logs_0518.zip (log bundle, 12MB)

Dana — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We're looking into this as P1. Quick notes / next actions from Redwood:

I'll host a quick ops -> eng sync at :45 (in 15 minutes) to align on an immediate plan. If we need exec attention, we'll escalate to a 10:30 CTO/ops briefing.

—Michael

Quick triage results (initial):

- Replayed 10 request IDs from the archive (IDs: elm-req-87f3, elm-req-87f4, elm-req-87f9...). All reproduce high latency; p95 ~1.9s locally against Elmbridge's private runtime snapshot.
- Profiling (attached profile_run_20260518.pdf) shows long delays in the CPU-based tokenizer/decoder stage rather than the GPU kernels themselves. The runtime hit path: larger-than-usual prefix tokens are bypassing prefix cache and causing repeated re-tokenization.
- Marcus found a recent small change in our tokenizer caching lookup that can cause O(N^2) behavior when a request contains long system prompts with embedded context markers. The change landed in the runtime on 2026-05-16 (commit sha: 8d3f2a).

Immediate mitigations proposed:
1) Roll the tokenizer-cache change back on Elmbridge's private control plane to the pre-2026-05-16 binary (fast rollback).
2) Canary a runtime with batch_size=1 and forced prefix cache warm-up for high-latency routes.
3) Apply a small hotfix (kfix_patch.diff) to short-circuit the pathological lookup in the tokenizer for long-prefix cases.

Risk assessment: rollback is low-risk and should restore p95 to baseline within 20–30 minutes if the tokenizer patch is causal. Canary + hotfix will reduce blast radius before a full rollout.

Requesting:
- Michael: permission to schedule rollback now and notify Elmbridge of a 30m expected remediation window.
- Marcus: prepare the rollback binary + hotfix branch and a canary config (reduced batch).

Naomi
Naomi Feldman | Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Attachments: profile_run_20260518.pdf (profiling summary), kfix_patch.diff (proposed hotfix)
